Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
Unemployment at 6.1% with a 12-month decline of 1.1pp points to mid-2014, when the rate was 6.1% in April–June 2014. The 10-year yield at 2.50% and the 2-year at 0.58% fit that period too.

The VIX at 15.98 with a 3-month rise of 4.41 suggests a spike from a low base. That fits October 2014, when the VIX hit about 26 intraday, but unemployment was 5.9% by then. September 2014 had unemployment at 5.9% and the 10-year near 2.5%, so the match isn't exact. Revisions could explain the gap, because the figures are "as known" and the rate may have been 6.1% in the data at that time.

Other cues:
- The dollar was up 5% over 3 months, consistent with the strong dollar rally of summer 2014.
- Gold fell 6.2% in the month, which fits September 2014.
- EM equity fell 7.8% and developed ex-US fell 3.9% in the month, which also fits September 2014.
- US large-cap equity at -1.4% for the month fits September 2014, when the S&P fell about 1.4%.
- The 2-year yield rose in September 2014 to about 0.58%, which fits.

Unemployment was reported as 6.1% for August 2014, released in early September, but the September report (5.9%) came out on October 3. If the snapshot used a lagged release, the rate would still read 6.1%. So September 2014 is the best match.
